name: Hourglass-Waste
geological_features: Hourglass-shaped canyon eroded between twin mesas
Sand seas with migrating dune formations
Exposed mineral veins in canyon walls
specific_features: Sand flows through the canyon narrows like an hourglass, cycling between basins
description: Hourglass-Waste takes its name from a massive canyon formation where two circular basins are connected by a narrow passage. Wind and gravity drive sand from one basin to the other through this passage in a cycle that takes approximately one local year, creating a geological hourglass visible from orbit.

The thin atmosphere does little to moderate the temperature extremes, and the low gravity allows sand to hang suspended in the air for hours after a wind event. Dust devils grow to enormous scale here, their weak gravity allowing columns of sand to reach several kilometers in height.

The canyon walls expose mineral veins laid down over billions of years of geological history, their cross-sections readable like a stratigraphic timeline. The hourglass flow has polished the narrow passage smooth, revealing crystal inclusions that sparkle in direct sunlight.

The mineral deposits visible in the canyon walls suggest more substantial resources at depth, but the shifting sand makes permanent installations difficult. The hourglass cycle itself has attracted interest from researchers studying granular dynamics and self-organizing geological systems.
